 Judgment

These appeals are directed against the judgment and award dated 01st February, 2020 passed in MVC No.2307 of 2018 on the File of the X Additional District Judge and Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi, (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal" for brevity).

entities.text: X Additional District Judge and Member
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Miscellaneous First Appeal No.101286 is preferred by claimants seeking enhancement of compensation and Miscellaneous First Appeal No.101238 is preferred by Insurance Company challenging the liability fixed on it.

Smt. Preeti Shashank, Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has submitted her arguments that the rider of the insured motorcycle had no licence to drive the same, so also, the rider of the motorcycle was charge-sheeted under Section 3 read with Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 for non-possession of Driving Licence.
She further submits that the charge sheet was available before the Tribunal.
The appellant had issued notice to the Driver and owner of the vehicle to produce the Driving Licence of the rider of the motorcycle.
The Tribunal has not considered the documents Exhibit R2-legal notice issued.
The Insurance Company has proved the violation of terms and conditions of the policy by the owner of the vehicle.
Hence, she submits that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

The learned counsel further submits that the Tribunal ought to have noticed the fact that the deceased also contributed to the accident by National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt.Meenaxi W/O Sanjeev Sanju Kalagade on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128201056/
3 riding the motorcycle on the road with having driving licence and insurance and hence, on all these grounds, sought to allow the appeal.
4.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt.Meenaxi W/O Sanjeev Sanju Kalagade
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As against the same, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant-claimants sought to justify the judgment and NC: 2023:KHC-D:9548-DB award and submits that the Tribunal has appreciated the evidence adduced and materials placed before it while awarding compensation.

It is further submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding just compensation and the compensation awarded is on the lower side and hence sought for enhancement of the compensation.
5.

In the light of the arguments advanced by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, the following points would arise for our consideration in this appeal:
1.
Whether the Insurance Company has made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the insurance company?
2. Whether the claimants have made out a case for enhancement of compensation?

6. Our answer for the above points are as under:
Point No.1: in the negative;
Point No.2: partly in the affirmative NC: 2023:KHC-D:9548-DB Regarding Point No.1:
7.
We have carefully reviewed the materials presented before this Court.
Based on the complaint filed by Basavaraj Yallappa Kelagade, the Ghataprabha Police registered a case in Crime No.333 of 2017 against the rider of a new HF Deluxe company motorcycle.
The charges were for offenses punishable under Section 279, 337, 338, and 304A of the Indian Penal Code, and a First Information Report (FIR) was subsequently submitted to the Court.

Following this, the Police promptly arrived at the scene, conducted a spot panchnama in the presence of witnesses (panchas)
as per Exhibit P3, prepared a rough sketch on-site, carried out an inquest panchnama, and executed a seizure panchnama.
They also obtained reports from the Motor Vehicle Inspector and the post-mortem report, and recorded statements from witnesses.

After a comprehensive investigation,
the Investigating Officer submitted a charge sheet against accused No.1, Mahantesh Siddappa Valadavar, and accused No.2, Siddappa Basavanni Valadavar.

The charges were related to offenses punishable under Sections 279, 338, and 304A of the Indian Penal Code, as well as Sections 3 read with 181 and Sections 5 read with 180, 146, and 196 of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9548-DB Motor Vehicles Act.
In addition to this documentary evidence, the appellants also presented the testimony of PW1.

Upon a thorough assessment of the evidence on record, the Tribunal rightfully concluded that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent actions of the motorcycle rider with registration No. KA-49/V-3817.

With regard to liability of the Insurance Company is concerned, in paragraph 15 of the judgment, the Tribunal has observed as under:
"Regarding liability:

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 has led the evidence of witness as RW.1 and marked Exs.R1 to R3.

The respondent No.1 has been cross-examined by the counsel for the petitioners, wherein the RW.1 has admitted that the policy issued was in force as on the date of the accident and also has admitted that the said police is package policy.
The RW.1 has stated that they have issued notice to respondent No.1 and the acknowledgement of notice is not produced.
The RW.1 has also admitted that they have not applied for licence particulars of respondent No.1 in the office of R.T.O.
The RW.1 has admitted that they have only collected police papers.

The respondent No.2 has not proved substantially that the respondent No.1 rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA.49/V-3817 was not possessing driving licence, except relying on the charge sheet filed by the police.

Though, the respondent No.2 has issued notice to produce the driving icence as per Exs.R2 and R3, the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9548-DB respondent No.2 has not produced the proof of service of the said notice sent by the respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 has failed to prove service of notice to respondent No.1.
The respondent No.2 has not taken any effective steps to call upon the respondent No.1 to produce the driving licence.

Whereas the respondent No.2 has filed I.A.
No.III calling upon the petitioners to produce the driving licence of the deceased.

The respondent No.2 has not made any efforts to call upon the respondent No.1 to produce the driving licence nor they have issued any notice to the RTO requesting for the driving licence particulars of the deceased.
Hence, the respondent No.2 has effectively failed to prove that the respondent No.1 was not possessing driving licence as on the date of the accident.

The respondent No.2 being the insurer of motor cycle and having failed to prove that the respondent No.1 was not possessing the driving licence, the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

The petitioners having proved the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA.49/V-3817 and as on the date of the accident, the said motor cycle was validly insured.

The respondent No.2 being the insurer of said motor cycle bearing No.KA.49/V-3817 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners together with interest at the rate of 06% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of entire amount to the petitioners within one month from the date of this order.
Accordingly, I answer the Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative."

Apart from above observation made by the Tribunal, we have also noticed that respondent-Insurance Company has not placed any material before the Tribunal that whether the Investigating Officer has issued Notice under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act to the owner of the vehicle to produce driving license of the offending vehicle and also the insurance policy.
The Insurance Company has also not complied with the mandatory provisions of Rule 232 of (duties of I n s u r a n c e C o m p a n y ) K a r n a t a k a M o t o r V e h i c l e R u l e s .

O n appreciation/re-appreciation/re-evaluation and reconsideration of the entire material placed before this Court, we are of the view that the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts.

Viewed from any angle, we do not find any legal National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt.Meenaxi W/O Sanjeev Sanju Kalagade on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128201056/
5 infirmities/illegalities in the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: Accordingly, we answer the Point No.1 in the negative.
9. As regards quantum of compensation is concerned, as per Exhibit P6 the age of the deceased is shown as 28 years.
PW1-wife of the deceased in her deposition has stated that the deceased was doing coolie work and earning Rs.15,000/- per - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9548-DB month.
But no documentary evidence is produced to prove the same.
Hence the notional income has to be taken.
The Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.9,000/- per month which is not in consonance of the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
According to the guidelines, for the accidents of the year 2017, the notional income is to be taken at Rs.10,250/-.

As per the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 40% is to be added to income as future prospects.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since there are two dependents, one-third has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.

As per the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS v. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER reported in (2009)6 SCC 121, for the age of 28 years, the appropriate multiplier would be 17.

entities.text: SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS v. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER reported in (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has adopted proper multiplier.
Accordingly, the loss of dependency would be Rs.19,51,668/- (Rs.9,576/- x 12 x 17).

As per the dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of PRANAY SETHY (supra) the claimants are entitled for Rs.80,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 2) towards loss of - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9548-DB consortium and Rs.15,000/- each towards loss of estate and towards funeral expenses.
In total, the claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.20,61,668/- as against Rs.17,83,600/- awarded by the Tribunal.
In the light of the discussion made above, we answer the Point No.2, partly in the affirmative.

In the result, we pass the following:

Miscellaneous First Appeal No.101238 of 2020 preferred by the Insurance is dismissed;

2. Miscellaneous First Appeal No.101286 of 2020 preferred by the claimants is allowed in part;
